card.name: Words leading up to "intentional" or "on purpose"
card.fires_on: The spot just before a word meaning "intentional" or "on purpose" is completed. This includes "on" before "purpose", "or" after "accidentally", and the start of "unintended" or "unintentional".

modes.label: Start of unintended/unintentional
modes.description: Partway through "unintended" or "unintentional" in warnings about exposure or overdose.
modes.example: OVERDOSAGE There is limited clinical trial experience regarding overdose with ZTALMY. Un<<int>>entional overdose has been reported in

modes.label: Accidental or intentional
modes.description: The word "or" after "accidental(ly)", where "intentional(ly)" comes next.
modes.example: OVERDOSAGE Note —For management of hypertensive crises see WARNINGS section. Accidental<< or>> intentional overdosage may be more common

modes.label: On purpose
modes.description: The word just before "purpose" is completed, in ordinary prose.
modes.example: Could the Egyptians have built the Giza pyramids that way<< on>> purpose?

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words meaning "intentional", "deliberately" and "purpose".
card.plain: It fires when the text is about to say that something was done on purpose, often right after "accidental or".
